title: Bechet's compositions
summary: Wilber recorded ten Bechet compositions and discusses Ghost of the Blues and the late French folk melodies.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: By the way, did Sidney have any other special numbers that he wrote that you can think of much that maybe didn't get on record?
Yeah, he did. Ghost of the Blues was one of his really good numbers that was written around 1924.
Lawson Seeley's picture on the cover.

Yeah. I made a recording this last year for a classic jazz label of Sidney's compositions. I picked out, I got a hold of all the music I could from Leeds and Clarence Williams and his various publishers and picked out about 10 of his best things.
And he wrote some beautiful things.
Ghost of the Blues is a marvelous tune. Black Stick.
Well, P. Ron recorded that, didn't he? Yeah. That's right.
Yeah. Didn't care much for that P. Ron recording. Still.
And what else? When the Sun Sets Down South.
And, well, there was a lot of things that he composed in his last years, 10 years, which were sort of folk melodies, but very nice little.
Yeah. Some of those things he did over in France. Yeah.
And they became big hits over there.
Yeah. Maybe some of the old Creole numbers. Yeah.
Some of them sold like over a million records.
